faqs.question: What does JC-BK Virus DNA Detection by Real-time PCR - Urine measure?
faqs.answer: This test detects the presence of JC polyoma and BK virus in your urine using the Real-Time PCR method.

faqs.question: Why is JC-BK Virus DNA Detection by Real-time PCR - Urine done?
faqs.answer: • To detect the presence of JC polyoma and BK viruses • To help patients with weakened immune systems due to conditions such as HIV • To oversee the immunity of people who have had an organ transplant or are undergoing chemotherapy

faqs.question: When is JC-BK Virus DNA Detection test recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: Your doctor may recommend this test if you have • a weakened immune system due to conditions such as HIV, • had an organ transplant or are undergoing chemotherapy, or • symptoms such as fever, urinary tract infections, or other symptoms suggestive of viral infections.

faqs.question: What if the results of the JC-BK Virus DNA Detection urine test are abnormal?
faqs.answer: If you test positive for JC polyoma or BK virus, it may indicate an active or past infection.

faqs.question: What to expect during the JC-BK Virus DNA Detection test?
faqs.answer: You will be asked to collect a 15ml spot urine sample in a sterile leak-proof container. The sample will be sent to the laboratory for testing.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the JC-BK Virus DNA Detection test?
faqs.answer: • Inform your doctor about any medications you are taking. • Follow any other instructions provided by your doctor and let them know if you have any specific requirements. • Provide details of your clinical history and clinician number.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with the JC-BK Virus DNA Detection test?
faqs.answer: Blood tests to check kidney function and overall health.

faqs.question: What is the JC-BK Virus DNA Detection by Real-time PCR - Urine also known as?
faqs.answer: Polyomavirus JC/BK DNA Quantitative PCR, JC and BK Virus, or JC/BK Quantitative Real-Time PCR

faqs.question: What are JC polyoma and BK viruses?
faqs.answer: JC polyoma and BK virus are common viruses that usually do not cause symptoms in healthy people. However, they can cause serious infections in people suffering from conditions such as HIV, organ transplant, or chemotherapy.
